topic: Quick comparisons: endorphins vs endocannabinoids, what causes the runner's high. Old belief = endorphins; blood beta-endorphin cannot cross the blood-brain barrier while lipid anandamide can; mice: anxiety relief and pain relief after running depend on cannabinoid receptors (Fuss et al., PNAS 2015); humans: 63 people, 45 min moderate treadmill run, opioid blocker naltrexone vs placebo, euphoria and lower anxiety still developed, anandamide and 2-AG rose (Siebers et al., Psychoneuroendocrinology 2021); but PET in 10 athletes after a 2-hour run showed brain opioid release that correlated with euphoria (Boecker et al., Cerebral Cortex 2008)

cards.html:
Myth check

Runner's high? Endorphins may not be the cause.

Fig. 1 · The problem

Endorphins are big peptides.

In your blood, they can't cross the blood-brain barrier.

Fig. 2 · Side by side

Can it pass from blood into the brain?

Endorphin

Peptide

Large

NO

Anand­amide

Fat-based

Small

YES

Anandamide is your body's own cannabis-like molecule.

Fig. 3 · The 2021 test

63

people ran for 45 minutes.

Half got a drug that blocks opioids, like endorphins.

The high still came.

Fig. 4 · Not so fast

Endorphins still help.

2008 brain scan: opioid release after a 2-hour run.

Top suspects now: endocannabinoids.

Save this for your next long run.
